# ethereum-optimism/infra Weekly Report (May 31 - June 6, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week’s activity centered on hardening the Superchain’s interoperability infrastructure, specifically focusing on recovery mechanisms for interop-related failures. The team identified critical operational bottlenecks in the `op-reth` transaction pool and initiated the development of a comprehensive runbook for handling invalid interop messages. Additionally, progress was made on establishing long-running devnets and aligning `op-revm` with upstream releases to support upcoming hardforks.

## 🛠️ Key Developments
While no new features or pull requests were finalized during this period, significant technical groundwork was laid in the following areas:

### Infrastructure & Devnet Progression
*   **Devnet Evolution:** The team successfully transitioned from a local devnet environment to an active effort to establish a long-running devnet. This represents a key step in providing a stable, persistent testing ground for the OP Stack ([#20691](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/20691)).
*   **EVM Compatibility:** Discussions regarding `op-revm` support focused on synchronizing with `revm` v111. This update is critical for maintaining compatibility with the Amsterdam hardfork and refactoring crates to allow for shared type definitions across the ecosystem ([#21069](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/21069)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage
The week's triage efforts highlighted vulnerabilities in how the sequencer handles failsafe events and reorgs within the interop framework.

### New & Active Issues
*   **Interop Transaction Pool Recovery:** A significant issue was identified where the `op-reth` interop transaction pool fails to resume after a failsafe is disabled. Investigation revealed that `op-rbuilder` (the reth-based builder) retains evicted state, necessitating a full restart of both `op-reth` and `op-rbuilder` on affected sequencers. To improve future response, a new metric has been proposed to make the failsafe state observable ([#21149](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/21149)).
*   **Protocol Security & Runbook Development:** Work has begun on a formal runbook for recovering a chain after an invalid interop message triggers a reorg. This effort aims to address the current system's inability to smoothly handle large reorgs and integrates several related issues ([#21161](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/21161), [#20006](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/20006), [#21125](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/issues/21125)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
Collaboration this week was highly focused on cross-component troubleshooting between `op-reth` and `op-rbuilder`. The technical dialogue suggests a tight feedback loop between infrastructure maintainers and protocol engineers as they navigate the complexities of interop failsafes. The community's focus on upstream `revm` releases indicates an active effort to remain aligned with the broader Ethereum execution layer roadmap while tailoring those tools for Optimism's specific Layer 2 requirements.
